summary:
What it is: An interactive desktop app for children aged 7–12 that simulates astronaut training and mission decision-making under pressure.

Core Loop (4 Steps):

Learn First: Age-appropriate knowledge cards based on real NASA facts.

Simulate: Navigating 6 mission stages (from ASCAN selection to launch).

Decide: Managing resources (Oxygen, Energy, Morale, Knowledge, Time) while facing high-stakes crisis trade-offs.

Learn from Consequences: Connecting decisions to real NASA science facts.

Key Features:

Real NASA Data: Uses live/archived APIs (DONKI, Mars InSight, OSDR, Artemis, Perseverance).

Integrated NASA Games: 8 embedded educational games linked to simulation stages.

Progression: Medal system, persistent skill trees, and a global leaderboard.

Accessibility: Two distinct difficulty modes for ages 7–9 and 10–12.

Communication Delay: Realistic deep-space communication lag (e.g., 20-minute delay on Mars missions).
details:
The Problem

Space education for children often stays too abstract — posters, general facts, and passive videos. Kids learn what happened in space, but never how astronauts actually think and decide. The real challenge of space exploration is not just the hardware — it is the decision-making under pressure, with limited resources and no room for error.

DORA bridges that gap.

What is DORA?

DORA (Dynamic Orbital Resource Academy) is an interactive desktop application built for children ages 7–12 that simulates real astronaut training and mission decision-making. It combines:

Structured space education — 5 progressive learning cards before any simulation begins

Engineering trade-off simulation — real resource management decisions with no free choice

8 integrated NASA games — real NASA-built games embedded directly into the platform

Reward and leaderboard system — medals, skills, and global rankings to drive replayability

How It Works

Step 1 — Learn First

Before the simulation begins, players go through 5 age-appropriate knowledge cards:

What is space? Who becomes an astronaut? What is the ISS? Why does resource management matter? Are you ready?

Each card uses plain language, real NASA facts, and visual storytelling designed for ages 7–12.

Step 2 — Simulate

Players manage a lunar or Martian outpost across 6 mission stages:

Stage Topic

1 ASCAN Selection — Medical and Reflexes

2 ISS Systems — Life Support

3 T-38 Flight — Cockpit and Survival

4 NBL Pool — Spacewalk Training

5 Canadarm2 — Robotics and Docking

6 Launch — Countdown and Orbit

Step 3 — Decide

Every stage presents a real crisis scenario with 3 choices. Each choice has a genuine cost — no option is free:

CRISIS: Solar flare detected!

A) Open radiation shield

Energy -30, Radiation protected

B) Continue science operations

Knowledge +40, Radiation exposure +25

C) Retreat to shielded module

Time -20, Oxygen +15

Resources tracked: Oxygen, Energy, Morale, Knowledge, Time

Step 4 — Learn from Consequences

Every decision triggers a real NASA science fact, connecting the in-game outcome to actual mission constraints. Children walk away understanding a real engineering trade-off, not just having played a fun game.

Real NASA Data Integration

DORA is grounded in real NASA open data, not invented statistics:

Data Source Usage in DORA

NASA DONKI API Live solar activity affects radiation scenarios

Mars InSight Data Real surface temperature displayed

NASA OSDR Astronaut health data informs resource mechanics

Artemis Mission Data Lunar south pole environment parameters

Perseverance Rover Mars Jezero Crater site conditions

When live data is unavailable, DORA transparently falls back to archived NASA datasets, clearly labeled as such within the application.

Integrated NASA Games

DORA embeds 8 real NASA-built educational games, accessible from the sidebar panel:

Snap It — Eclipse Photography

CubeSat Builder — Satellite Engineering

Explore Mars — Rover Navigation and Coding

Go With the Flow — Ocean Currents Science

DSN Uplink-Downlink — Deep Space Communications

Helios — Solar Energy and Fusion

Games are connected to simulation stages. Completing a game reinforces the knowledge introduced in the corresponding training stage.

Motivation and Replayability

Medal System

Every stage completed earns a medal based on performance:

Gold — both resource bars above 70%

Silver — bars between 40 and 70%

Bronze — completed but critically low resources

Medals accumulate across multiple playthroughs and are never reset. Players can always improve their score by replaying with a better strategy.

Skill Tree

Each completed stage unlocks a permanent passive bonus that carries into future runs. For example, completing the ISS Systems stage unlocks Energy Management, which reduces energy cost on all subsequent decisions. This rewards learning and incentivizes replay.

Global Leaderboard

A built-in leaderboard ranks all players by gold medal count, total knowledge points, and mission completion speed. Players can filter by category, encouraging different kinds of mastery.

Difficulty and Accessibility

DORA supports two difficulty modes:

Easy Mode (ages 7–9)

Knowledge cards are mandatory before simulation

Two decision options per crisis instead of three

Simplified language throughout

Less punishing resource penalties

Normal Mode (ages 10–12)

Knowledge cards can be skipped

Three decision options per crisis

Technical terms included with brief in-context explanations

Full resource management system active

This design allows the same application to serve a full classroom with mixed age groups, as well as home use with parents and older siblings.

Communication Delay Mechanic

One of the most distinctive features of DORA is the communication delay system, directly inspired by real deep space mission constraints. When players are on a Mars mission, messages from Earth arrive 20 minutes late. Players must decide whether to follow outdated instructions or trust their own judgment — exactly the dilemma real Mars mission planners face today.
